result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [sdtm_to_metadata()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: Convert an SDTM domain template to a MetadataImport object. twitter-card: title: >- [sdtm_to_metadata()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: Convert an SDTM domain template to a MetadataImport object. title: >- [sdtm_to_metadata()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Convert an SDTM domain template to a MetadataImport object. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Convert an SDTM domain template to a `MetadataImport` object. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_sdtm_validate.py#L35-L156){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature sdtm_to_metadata( domain, study_id=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The SDTM domain templates (see [`get_sdtm_domain()`](`pointblank.get_sdtm_domain`)) have their own classes, [`SDTMDomainTemplate`](`pointblank.SDTMDomainTemplate`) and [`SDTMVariableSpec`](`pointblank.SDTMVariableSpec`). The `sdtm_to_metadata()` function converts a template to a [`MetadataImport`](`pointblank.MetadataImport`), the same object that [`import_metadata()`](`pointblank.import_metadata`) returns for a metadata file. That gives the template the methods of a `MetadataImport`, such as [`to_schema()`](`pointblank.MetadataImport.to_schema`) and [`get_variable()`](`pointblank.MetadataImport.get_variable`), and lets it be exported with [`export_metadata()`](`pointblank.export_metadata`). Each variable in the template becomes a [`VariableMetadata`](`pointblank.VariableMetadata`) with the same name, label, role, `required` flag, maximum length and controlled terminology name. SDTM's `"Num"` type becomes the `"Float64"` dtype and `"Char"` becomes `"String"`. The dataset name and label come from the domain, and the source version is `"IG 3.4"`. The template names the codelist of a variable (as in `controlled_term="SEX"`) but doesn't contain the codelist itself, so the result has no codelists. Calling `import_metadata(format="cdisc_sdtm", domain=...)` gives the same result. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [domain]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The SDTM domain code, such as `"DM"`, `"AE"` or `"LB"`. This is case-insensitive. [study_id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A study identifier to record in the metadata's `study_id`. The default is `None`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [MetadataImport]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The metadata for the domain, with `source_format="cdisc_sdtm"`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If there is no template for the domain. See [`list_sdtm_domains()`](`pointblank.list_sdtm_domains`) for the domains that have one. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's convert the template for the Demographics (DM) domain: ::: {#40d4e205 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb dm_meta = pb.sdtm_to_metadata("DM", study_id="STUDY01") print(dm_meta.dataset_label) print(dm_meta.source_version) print(dm_meta.variable_names[:6]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Demographics IG 3.4 ['STUDYID', 'DOMAIN', 'USUBJID', 'SUBJID', 'RFSTDTC', 'RFENDTC'] ``` ::: ::: The metadata has all 26 variables of the template, in the template's order. Each variable keeps what the template says about it: ::: {#9514ac75 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} sex = dm_meta.get_variable("SEX") print(sex.dtype, sex.required, sex.max_length, sex.controlled_term) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` String True 2 SEX ``` ::: ::: `SEX` is a required character variable of at most two characters, with values from the `SEX` codelist of CDISC Controlled Terminology. The metadata can be turned into a [`Schema`](`pointblank.Schema`) for use in [`Validate.col_schema_match()`](`pointblank.Validate.col_schema_match`): ::: {#7056e660 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} schema = dm_meta.to_schema() schema.columns[:4] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [('STUDYID', 'String'), ('DOMAIN', 'String'), ('USUBJID', 'String'), ('SUBJID', 'String')] ``` ::: ::: The schema lists every variable of the template, including the expected and permissible ones. A real DM dataset usually has only some of them, so a schema check against all 26 is stricter than SDTM requires. For checking a dataset against the template, [`validate_sdtm()`](`pointblank.validate_sdtm`) (which only checks the variables that are present) is usually the better fit. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~get_sdtm_domain`) : Get the template that is converted. [](`~validate_sdtm`) : Build a validation plan from an SDTM domain template. [](`~adam_to_metadata`) : The equivalent for ADaM dataset templates. [](`~MetadataImport`) : The object that is returned.
